subject: Budget thresholds & unit-rate recap — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Budget thresholds & unit-rate recap — post-demo follow-up

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the numbers we discussed so the team can align on next steps: 

- Estimated monthly query volume: 120M tokens (peak) / 60M tokens (steady).
- Typical sequence length we observed in your sample: ~220 tokens.
- Target budget range you gave on the call: $8k–$25k/month.
- Unit economics target you mentioned: ~$7–$12 per 1M tokens (all-in after caching/batching).

I created a conservative invoice sketch and a simple token unit economics CSV showing 3 scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive). Attached: redwood_invoice_estimate_heliX_v1.xlsx and token_unit_econ_breakdown.csv. Short notes on assumptions in the spreadsheet: 5–15% effective prefix caching, batch windows optimized for 95th percentile latency, and using a CPU+quantized model fallback for non-critical workloads.

Next steps I propose: 
1) You confirm the monthly token bands (steady vs peak) and any hard budget ceilings we should respect.
2) If procurement needs a separate breakdown, I can generate a one-page invoice-ready summary for finance.
3) If the numbers look reasonable, we can schedule a quick internal technical sync (30m) to validate latency SLOs and KV-cache sizing.

If helpful, I highlighted two lines in the spreadsheet that map to a $10/1M tokens mid-case and to a $7/1M tokens experimental configuration. Would love to know which lane you prefer.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_invoice_estimate_heliX_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)
Attachment: token_unit_econ_breakdown.csv (CSV, 6KB)

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@helixhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Budget thresholds & unit-rate recap — post-demo follow-up

Evelyn —

Thanks for the summary and the files. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- The 120M tokens peak is accurate for a launch week burst; steady-state is closer to 55–65M tokens/month.
- Finance wants to see a 12-month spend projection (monthly buckets + anticipated growth). Can you include both steady and burst scenarios per month?
- Our procurement contact is looped in (procurement@helixhealth.com). They’ll need an invoice-style line item breakdown (unit price per 1M tokens, estimated monthly spend, and a clause for overage billing).

On price range: I liked the mid-case math at $10/1M tokens, but Finance asked whether a multi-tier model (volume bands with lower unit price above 200M tokens) is possible. Is that something you can.surface in the next draft?

Also: any compliance notes we should add for SOC 2 and data retention (we will ask security later).

—Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Integrations, Helix Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, procurement@helixhealth.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:52:00 -0800
Subject: Revised invoice + 12-month projection and tiered-band option

Samira / procurement team —

Per your ask, I updated the workbook and added: 
- A 12-month projection tab with steady vs launch-week burst months.
- A tiered pricing option: $11/1M tokens up to 200M, $8/1M tokens thereafter (reduces unit cost materially for scale).
- An invoice-style one-pager ("Helix — Redwood Invoice Estimate") for procurement with clearly labeled line items and an overage clause.

Summary numbers (monthly mid-case at $10/1M):
- Steady month (60M tokens): $600/month estimated (this is illustrative; spreadsheet shows rounding and network costs).
- Launch month (120M tokens): $1,200 estimated.
- 12-month mid-case total: $10,200 (includes two projected launch months).

Notes and assumptions included in the attached workbook at the top of each tab. I also exported a PNG snapshot of the pricing-calculator worksheet (pricing_calculator_snapshot.png) for quick sharing.

Do you want this as a formal quote (PDF) for signatures, or is an invoice-estimate draft sufficient for procurement to open a PO? If procurement wants a quote we can route to finance for an SLA note.

I can also loop in our security lead for SOC 2 / data retention language once procurement confirms PO timing.

Best,
Evelyn

Attachment: redwood_invoice_estimate_heliX_v1.xlsx (updated, XLSX, 58KB)
Attachment: pricing_calculator_snapshot.png (PNG, 18KB)
Attachment: token_unit_econ_breakdown.csv (CSV, 6KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Revised invoice + 12-month projection and tiered-band option

Evelyn / team —

Quick internal note and approve-to-send: the math looks clean. Two small asks before we send a formal quote: 
1) Add a one-line SLA credit language (72h incident response, 99.5% uptime) to the one-pager.
2) In the tiered band table, call out the exact rounding method (we use monthly-aggregate rounding to nearest 1M tokens).

Evelyn — once those two lines are in place, please convert to PDF and tag as "quote for PO" and I’ll approve. CC-ing Samira so procurement can confirm preferred PO terms.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
